name: Intelligence / ISR Analysis
sw_tam: ~$10–20B intel/ISR-analysis software; Palantir gov the anchor (co. Q2'26 rev $1.9B, +93% YoY, filings-verified — much of it government)
htc: none — sovereign/clearance-gated and Palantir-captured (D=5). Vannevar Labs is the exception but late-stage. Only adjacency is commercial-OSINT / dual-use intel tooling that avoids the clearance wall.
falsi: By 2027, does DoD/IC field a program-of-record agent producing >X% of first-draft intel products (vs analyst-copilot)? Until PED billets are actually cut, Additive/Expansion holds.
anti: Net is Expansion, not displacement: the IC is chronically understaffed and clearance-gated, so AI expands analytic throughput against a latent un-triaged backlog rather than cutting billets. And it is nearly uninvestable at seed — Palantir owns the sovereign layer outright.
players: Palantir (Gotham/AIP — sovereign-captured, D=5), Vannevar Labs (operational intel software, the rare venture-scale independent), Anduril (Lattice ISR), Scale AI (Donovan), Helsing (Cirra real-time radar-threat analysis), Primer. Palantir gov revenue is filings-verified.

name: Autonomous Defense Systems & Logistics
sw_tam: tens of $B defense-autonomy capex/RaaS (NOT a coupled wage-bill); Anduril ~$2.2B rev '25 → ~$4.3B proj '26, $20B Army ceiling contract
htc: none at seed — the category has already minted $12–61B independent primes; capex + programs-of-record favor scaled players. Adjacent seed only in subsystems/propulsion/sim/data; physical + R5 puts it on a robotics/procurement clock, capture <1%.
falsi: By 2027, does a NATO military formally cut a manned-platform program or billets in favor of autonomous systems? Recruiting-shortfall backfill = Expansion; actual billet cuts = the Compression flip.
anti: Net is Expansion, not Compression: Western militaries face recruiting shortfalls, so autonomy backfills UNFILLED billets rather than cutting heads — and the headline 'TAM' is procurement capex, not a coupled wage-bill (realized labor capture <1%). Treating Anduril's $61B valuation as displaced labor is the canonical physical-track hype error.
players: Anduril (Lattice/Fury/Arsenal-1; ~$2.2B rev '25, $61B val Series H, $20B Army ceiling — the revenue anchor), Shield AI (Hivemind autonomy, $12.7B val, $2B Series G), Helsing ($18B val, $1.8B raise, Centaur/Cirra), Saronic (maritime). Revenue (~$2.2B Anduril) is real; the $12–61B valuations are NOT labor proxies.

name: Screen & Video Production
sw_tam: ~$0.5–1B AI-video ARR; Runway ~$300M ARR the Western anchor (OpenAI Sora SHUT DOWN Mar'26: $2.1M lifetime rev vs $15M/day burn)
htc: Runway late-stage ($5.3B). Seed door in verticalized production workflow (ad/social video factories, dubbing/localization, game cinematics) and rights-cleared/licensed-data models — NOT foundation video. IP-litigation gate is live.
falsi: By 2027, does a major studio/streamer ship a flagship title with disclosed AI-driven VFX/crew-headcount reduction? Ad/social is already compressing; premium remains gated by IP + guild rules.
anti: Sora's shutdown is the tell: consumer text-to-video is NOT a business by itself — value accrues to workflow-embedded tools (Runway) and the commodity ad/social tier, while premium is IP/guild-gated. Displacement is real only in the low-end. And Chinese models (Kling at 30–40% cost) commoditize the model layer toward oss-style deflation.
players: Runway ($300M ARR, $5.3B val, Lionsgate/AMC deals — verified Western anchor), Google Veo 3.1 (native audio), Kuaishou Kling 3.0 (80–90% quality @ 30–40% cost), Pika, Luma. OpenAI Sora discontinued Mar–Apr 2026 (cautionary: consumer text-to-video isn't a standalone business).

Voice/dubbing (ElevenLabs) — not music generation — is the durable displacement wedge. Commodity/library tier compresses; premium/artist tier is Additive/Expansion.
players: ElevenLabs (voice/dubbing — verified-ARR spine, the durable wedge), Suno (music; WMG settled Nov'25), Udio (UMG settled Oct'25; Sony still suing over 30k songs, ruling expected summer'26; GEMA won in Munich Jul'26), Google Lyria, Inworld (game audio). name: Autonomous AI R&D Labs ('AI that builds AI')
labor_tam: ~$20-40B [L] — elite frontier AI-research wage bill (low tens of thousands of researchers globally at $450-500k+ base; US employs ~59% of elite researchers by top-conference pubs, China ~30k active). Mostly LATENT/net-new research-capacity expansion (Mirendil thesis: 'frontier R&D within reach of universities'), not a displaced wage bill. Derived fresh; near-null displacement denominator wrapped in [L] optionality.
sw_tam: ~$1-3B and mostly indirect: the labs themselves are pre-revenue frontier shops raising $100M-$2B seeds. The real SW-TAM is the picks-and-shovels floor — Prime Intellect ($100M+ ARR verified, RL post-training/sandboxes/eval), Thinking Machines Tinker.
htc: None as a lab — $100M-$2B seeds, ex-frontier-lab founders, L=5 lab-captured, pre-revenue at valuations detached from revenue. The only accessible surface is the infra floor (Prime Intellect-style RL/eval/sandbox picks-and-shovels), which lives in the SW-TAM ledger / W8, not in this track.
falsi: By Q4 2027: does an AI-R&D-automation lab (Core Automation/Mirendil/TML) ship a system that autonomously produces a reproducible, peer-recognized frontier ML result (e.g., new SOTA algorithm) with disclosed human-hours <10% of baseline? Yes -> 'AI builds AI' is real (L stays 5, still uninvestable at seed/A); No / still research-assist -> category is over-valued frontier-lab speculation with valuations detached from delivered automation.
anti: Consensus and the froth (Core Automation $4B six weeks post-launch, Mirendil $1B seed, TML $12B) treat 'AI that builds AI' as the highest-value frontier. Two corrections: (1) as a LABOR-TAM track it is a near-null denominator — tiny elite headcount wrapped in [L] latent optionality; the dollars are valuation, not a captured wage bill. (2) It is the single most lab-captured cell in the map (L=5) — uninvestable at seed/A for an outside fund; the only accessible value is the infra floor. P1's call to keep it a W8 watch-line rather than a full track was correct; promoting it risks importing valuation-as-TAM.
players: Core Automation (Jerry Tworek, ex-OpenAI VP Research; $100M @ $1B, then eyeing $300-500M @ $4B target ~6 weeks post-launch, 2026 — target, not closed), Mirendil (ex-Anthropic Neyshabur/Mehta; $200M seed @ $1B, a16z/Kleiner Perkins/Nvidia, 2026), Thinking Machines Lab (Mira Murati; $2B seed @ $12B, Tinker product), Discovery Loop (Jeff Dean/Google, internal). ALL essentially pre-revenue — valuations are NOT revenue. Infra floor (accessible): Prime Intellect $100M+ ARR verified.

name: Scientific / Materials R&D Automation (AI scientists + self-driving labs + EDA)
labor_tam: ~$100-200B [W] + large [L] discovery-expansion tail — displaceable R&D scientist / lab-technician / design-verification-engineer wage bill across materials, chemistry, pharma-discovery and EDA, advanced-economy-weighted; the [L] tail (discovery that was never staffed) is much larger and unpriceable. Derived fresh.
sw_tam: ~$3-8B emerging: agentic EDA (ChipAgents — Series A expanded to $134M, 6x ARR growth H1 2026, 120+ deployments, 50%+ design-cycle reduction; ARR LEVEL UNVERIFIED, only growth-rate + deployment count disclosed) + self-driving-lab platforms + AI-for-science compute.
htc: The EDA/design-verification wedge is the most investable cell in the whole R&D cluster — coupled displacement of verification engineers, V=4, real ARR growth, below-incumbent (Synopsys/Cadence) — but ChipAgents is already at Series A $134M, so hunt adjacent verification/test/DV point-solutions at seed. Physical self-driving labs (Lila ~$8.5B reported, Periodic $300M) are capital-intensive, robotics/regulation-gated and largely inaccessible at seed.
falsi: By Q4 2027: does ChipAgents (or an EDA-agent peer) disclose >$50M VERIFIED ARR with net design-verification-engineer headcount reductions at >=3 named semiconductor customers -> coupled EDA displacement is real and startup-ownable; if Synopsys/Cadence embed equivalent agentic verification as a platform feature and independents stall -> verdict flips to incumbent. Separately, if a self-driving lab (Lila/Periodic) delivers a commercialized, third-party-replicated novel material/superconductor -> the [L] discovery-expansion thesis validates.
anti: Consensus bundles all 'AI for science' into one hype basket at frontier-lab valuations (Lila reportedly $8.5B, Periodic $300M pre-product). I split the track: the COMPUTATIONAL VERIFICATION slice (EDA — ChipAgents 6x ARR growth, 120 deployments, coupled displacement of verification engineers, V=4) is a real, near-term, coupled, startup-ownable labor-displacement cell — the most investable in the R&D cluster. The PHYSICAL wet-lab DISCOVERY slice is capital-intensive, robotics-gated (P), regulation-gated (pharma R=5) and mostly [L] latent expansion whose valuations run an order ahead of replicated results. Treating them as one bet is the error: EDA is coupled-Compression-and-investable; physical discovery is [L]-Expansion-and-capital-intensive.
players: EDA/semiconductor (strongest commercial signal): ChipAgents (Series A -> $134M, 6x ARR growth H1 2026, 120+ deployments; ARR level unverified) vs incumbents Synopsys/Cadence. Materials/chemistry: Periodic Labs ($300M seed, Fedus ex-OpenAI + Cubuk ex-DeepMind; superconductors + chip-thermal materials), Lila Sciences ($550M raised, $350M Series A Oct 2025, REPORTEDLY raising @ $8.5B — unconfirmed, Flagship/Nvidia). Drug discovery: Recursion, Arctoris, Isomorphic. Valuations >> revenue throughout; ChipAgents is the clearest commercial traction but ARR unverified.

The productivity gain is captured INSIDE MBB/Big-4 via captive platforms (Lilli, Gene); a startup selling 'AI strategy' competes with the client's own tools and lacks the trust/relationship moat. (b) Watch MBB aggregate consulting (non-AI-engineer) headcount in FY2026-27 reporting — BCG's grew in 2025 on AI-engineer tilt; if total advisory headcount turns down YoY, leverage-pyramid compression is confirmed.

sw_tam: ~$0.7–0.9B identifiable pure-play agent ARR (AlphaSense-anchored); low-single-digit $B category incl. incumbent-embedded AI
capture: Gross seat-penetration ~0.12–0.15% (~$0.7–0.9B ARR / $450–600B pool); coupled/displacement capture ≈ near-zero (<0.05%) — the revenue is additive seat-ARR on still-employed senior analysts/PMs; real headcount displacement is confined to the junior IB/research rung.
htc: Core horizontal analyst-copilot layer = proven/late — AlphaSense $7.5B, Rogo $2B, Hebbia $700M all past seed/A. Seed/A only survives in un-crowned sub-verticals (private-markets/PE, credit, insurance-investment research agents) or the auditable proprietary-data/eval layer feeding them, ~$20–60M post — but Daloopa-style data-infra is already at Series C. Practically: "none in the horizontal copilot — proven/late-stage; hunt un-crowned finance sub-verticals or the data/eval layer." Falsifier for the entry: an incumbent data owner (Bloomberg/FactSet/S&P/AlphaSense) ships the vertical agent natively first.
falsi: By Q4-2027: (1) BLS OEWS US financial-&-investment-analyst (13-2051) headcount — flat-to-up toward the +7% 2025–35 path (>360k) confirms Additive/Expansion; a fall below ~340k flips the track to Compression. (2) Outcome-priced/autonomous finance-analysis ARR ≥25% of category seat-ARR (from ~0 today) → coupling is real, formalize Mixed-coupled. (3) If 2027 bulge-bracket IB analyst intake classes recover toward pre-2025 size, the AI-attribution of the 2026 two-thirds cuts is falsified (macro, not AI).
anti: Consensus (Jun-2026 headlines): "AI is replacing Wall Street analysts — junior classes cut two-thirds." Contrarian: the dollar-weighted mass of the $450–600B pool is senior/PM judgment + fiduciary sign-off + client relationship — additive, and BLS projects the occupation GROWS +7% (2025–35). The cuts are real but entry-comp (dollar-light) and macro-confounded; the vendor revenue (AlphaSense $600M) is seat-augmentation, not outcome-priced displacement — banking it as displacement is the ~10x error the framework flags (line 343). Second-order contrarian: the durable moat is the proprietary DATA (Bloomberg/FactSet/S&P/AlphaSense; D=4), not the agent — so even where the labor thesis is right, startups get captured by incumbents.

name: Marketing & Content Creation
sw_tam: ~$3-5B realized AI-content SW today (AI copywriting category ~$3.5B, ->~$8B by 2033); report-mill '$30B agentic marketing content layer' claim should be discounted. Real vendor ARR modest and in some cases DECLINING (Jasper).
htc: None for horizontal copy (Jasper is the cautionary GPT-wrapper unwind — ARR contracting). Narrow durable wedge only in enterprise brand-governance/compliance (Writer, already past seed at $1.9B) or regulated/vertical content. Seed door effectively closed on horizontal content; frontier labs own the base layer free.

Watch WPP/Omnicom/Dentsu FY2026 aggregate headcount — already >=18k agency cuts in 18mo, WPP -1,000 more by end-2026 (to ~97,388); continued decline confirms coupled displacement at the production rung.

Anti-consensus: horizontal content is the MOST lab-captured, least-defensible app category — Jasper's revenue is FALLING ($120M->$88M) while the category 'grows.' Durable value is not in generating copy (labs do it free) but in (a) enterprise governance/brand-safety (Writer) and (b) the coupled displacement of agency production labor (WPP-style cuts), which accrues to advertisers as savings, not to content-tool startups.
players: Jasper (~$88M ARR, DOWN from ~$120M in 2023; val cut to ~$1.2-1.8B; GPT-wrapper unwind, founder exodus — single-source ARR, flag directional), Writer ($1.9B val, enterprise knowledge-graph + governance moat = the surviving niche), Copy.ai (380k+ users, many free), HubSpot (agentic marketing stack), Adobe/Canva (incumbent tool capture); frontier labs (ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude) are the L5 commoditizer.

name: Enterprise Knowledge Research & Synthesis
labor_tam: $100-200B (time-slice of knowledge-worker research/synthesis labor across the enterprise; a soft denominator, not a clean occupation)

Watch freelance-design marketplace (Upwork/Fiverr) creative-gig volumes/rates — sustained decline = coupled deflation of commodity production design materializing.

Anti-consensus: design is where INCUMBENTS have most decisively captured the AI wave by shipping it as a feature — Canva is already a top-5 global AI service. Startup TAM at the horizontal layer is near-zero; the real economic event is deflation of commodity production-design labor (stock, layout, basic assets), captured by the tool incumbents and their users, not by new entrants.

The only durable opening is horizontal cross-tool orchestration, whose economics are unproven (agent-washing, pilot-to-production chasm). Most 'coordination labor' displaced is a diffuse time-slice across many roles, not a clean occupation — so coupled displacement is real but slow and hard to capture.

name: Translation, Localization & Interpretation
sw_tam: ~$1.2–1.6B identifiable vendor ARR
capture: ~2–4% (identifiable translation-specific vendor ARR ~$1.2–1.6B ÷ ~$50–70B linguist wage bill). But 'capture' understates displacement here: the defining dynamic is deflation-to-~$0 via free MT, so most of the compressed value is captured by NO vendor — it evaporates rather than transferring.
htc: None — commodity/oss-deflated, model-lab-captured, seed door closed. The frozen High conviction is on the DISPLACEMENT direction, not on investability: the money evaporates rather than accruing to a startup, so there is no wage-bill transfer to price a seed/A against. The only theoretically seed-able angle is AI-native real-time interpretation for regulated language-access (medical/court/ASL) with human-in-loop escalation + QA — but proven incumbents (LanguageLine, Propio, GLOBO, Boostlingo) already hold certification and distribution moats, making any check Series B+ consolidation, not seed/A. RECOMMENDATION: PASS as a standalone track; use the DeepL / Fiverr / Upwork / BLS prints as a real-time deflation leading-indicator for the broader knowledge-work coupling model.
falsi: By Q4 2027: BLS OEWS 27-3091 employment prints below ~74,000 (from ~78,300 in 2023) AND Upwork translation-category demand remains ≥20% below its 2023 baseline → structural compression confirmed, hold Net=Compression. CONVERSELY, if BLS headcount holds ≥78k because language-access-mandated interpretation demand (ACA §1557 / Title VI, court/medical certification) offsets bulk-translation losses, the compression is confined to written translation and the interpretation wage floor holds → reweight Net toward Mixed. Secondary tell: DeepL 2026 ARR growth prints below +25% (vs 40–60% guided) → confirms even the leader is losing pricing to free LLMs.
anti: Consensus: 'AI is killing translators — massive, investable disruption.' Both halves are half-wrong for an allocator. (1) The displacement is real but UNINVESTABLE at the MT/localization layer: value deflates to ~$0 via free Google/Meta/LLM translation rather than transferring to a capturable vendor — even category-leader DeepL just cut 25% of staff, so there is no wage-bill capture to underwrite. This is the purest 'compression-without-transfer' cell in the knowledge-work families. (2) The durable, arguably GROWING pocket is real-time high-stakes interpretation (medical/legal/court/ASL), where language-access LAW simultaneously mandates human-quality access AND blocks full automation — regulation creates demand, inverting the 'translation = doomed' story. So: written translation is a deflation story to avoid; interpretation is a regulated-demand story, but one already owned by incumbents.
players: Google Translate / Meta SeamlessM4T / OpenAI real-time / Gemini

name: Customer Support & Service Resolution
sw_tam: ~$0.7–1.3B realized CX-agent ARR (2026)
capture: ~7–11% per-deployment (Sierra ~11%, Fin ~7%, Decagon ~4–11%). Aggregate realized track displacement only ~1–3% of the pool (BPO-operator ~2% revenue headwind is the audited floor). Capture ≠ deflection: genuine resolution 30–60% (Gartner ~14% full self-service), not vendor-claimed 76–80%.
htc: None for horizontal English enterprise CX — seed door closed (Sierra $15.8B, Decagon $4.5B, Fin acquired by Salesforce $3.6B). Proven anchor. Only seed-viable adjacency: verticalized, compliance-heavy CX (Gradient Labs profile — regulated financial services, healthcare, insurance) where audited-resolution + regulatory compliance is a moat horizontal agents can't cross, at seed–A ~$15–40M pre; plus non-English/emerging-market (LATAM/Africa) CX geo-arbitrage. Voice-for-physical-industries CX sits in W3.6, not here.
falsi: By Q4-2027 (FY27 operator guidance): combined Teleperformance + Concentrix organic revenue growth < −5% YoY = aggregate CX displacement accelerating past the hybrid equilibrium → Compression confirmed at scale, raise displacement conviction. Flat-to-positive = AI headwind capped by volume growth / hybrid reversion holds → Mixed persists. Corroborator: audited genuine-resolution on complex/regulated tickets clears 65% (vs 30–60% today) by Q4-2027 → capture-expansion real.
anti: Consensus: 'AI resolves ~80% of support; contact centers are uninvestible/dead.' Anti-consensus on three counts: (1) 80% is DEFLECTION not resolution — genuine resolution is 30–60% (Gartner ~14% full self-service), 15–25% of deflections are wrong, and <10% of enterprise deployments clear POC (Klarna rehired; Agentforce ~6% adoption). (2) The REAL displacement is not in-house seat elimination but BPO offshore-wage-arbitrage margin compression — visible only in audited operator guidance (TP/Concentrix), not vendor press releases. (3) Value capture is flowing to INCUMBENTS (Salesforce buying Fin, Agentforce riding CRM distribution), so the hottest category is simultaneously the most over-claimed on displacement AND the least investable at seed. The durable end-state is Klarna's own 'human-as-VIP' hybrid, not zero humans.

name: Outbound Sales Development (SDR/BDR)
sw_tam: ~$150–250M defensible pure-play ARR
capture: ≈0% coupled. Autonomous-SDR retained ARR (<$30M across 11x/Artisan/AiSDR) ÷ $100–150B wage bill = <0.03%. The real wage-bill erosion (~mid-single-digit %, attrition-driven) is captured by ADDITIVE augment tooling (Clay/incumbents), not by an outcome-priced displacement vendor — so coupled capture is functionally zero.
htc: None on the core coupled thesis. The autonomous-SDR seed door is closed (category discredited; 11x/Artisan cautionary; coupled capture ≈0), and the augment winner (Clay, $5B / $150M ARR) is far past seed and additive, not the displacement thesis HTC underwrites. The only defensible adjacent seed/A entry is VERTICAL outbound where owned proprietary data + deliverability/identity create a real moat (the HappyRobot-in-freight analog; cross-ref W3.6∩W9.2/W6.4 operational voice-agents) — underwrite retained-ARR and churn, never bookings. Horizontal autonomous SDR: pass.
falsi: By Q4 2027: does ANY pure-play autonomous AI-SDR vendor reach ≥$50M NET-RETAINED ARR with <30% annual logo churn and disclosed NRR >100% (genuinely productionized)? YES → autonomous coupled capture is finally real; re-rate Net→Compression, conviction→Medium. NO (11x/Artisan/AiSDR stay sub-$20M retained, >40% churn; hybrid pod remains standard) → autonomous thesis confirmed dead, capture stays ≈0. Labor cross-check: if SDR/BDR headcount falls >15% cumulatively by end-2027 AND the cut shifts from attrition to attributable autonomous replacement → displacement accelerates; if it stays attrition-driven and <15% → slow/augment-mediated compression confirmed.
anti: The 2024–25 consensus ("AI will replace the SDR"; >$2.7B into GTM-AI) inverted: autonomous SDR is the single clearest failure-to-productionize in the agent map — YET the SDR wage bill IS eroding. Contrarian read: the capital chased the wrong layer. Durable value in "AI for outbound" accrued to the additive data-orchestration workbench (Clay, $150M ARR / $5B, augment-priced) and to incumbents — NOT to the outcome-priced autonomous seat-replacement the category was sold as. Corollary: the report-mill "$5–5.8B AI-SDR market, 21–32% CAGR" is mostly Clay/Apollo/Outreach/ZoomInfo augment revenue rebadged as "autonomous SDR" — reject as a displacement proxy. And the incumbent that "owned" the data (ZoomInfo) still collapsed 97% — proof the moat is orchestration + deliverability, not raw data ownership.
players: Incumbents (Salesforce Agentforce SDR, HubSpot Breeze, Apollo, Outreach, Salesloft, ZoomInfo)

name: Sales Closing & Account Mgmt (B2B AE)
labor_tam: $0.8–1.2T [W] — B2B account-executive + account-management + field-sales comp; large, durable-seat pool. Confirmed frozen.
sw_tam: ~$8–12B sales-AI/revenue-intelligence software 2026 (rev-intel ~$3.8B'24→$5.4B'28; AI-in-sales $8.8B'25→$63.5B'32 @ ~33% CAGR). Real anchor: Gong ARR >$500M May'26 (+55% YoY). Overwhelmingly seat/copilot, not coupled.
htc: none — additive copilot on durable AE seats (Expansion, not coupled capture); incumbent-captured (Gong >$500M ARR, Clari, Salesforce/HubSpot own the CRM graph). No seed wage-bill-displacement wedge.
falsi: By Q4 2027: does any AI-AE vendor disclose commission-replacing OUTCOME pricing (≥20% of rev-intelligence ARR coupled to closed deals) AND US BLS sales-rep headcount turn flat-to-down? Both → flip to coupled/Compression. Absent → stays additive/Expansion (base case).
anti: Consensus: 'autonomous AI AE' replaces quota-carriers imminently. Disagree — closing is trust/relationship-gated (H=4, V=2), the SDR cohort already collapsed (11x 70–90% churn), AE is harder. Value is additive copilot (Expansion); the real money is Gong-style rev-intelligence riding durable seats, not seat elimination.
players: Gong (ARR >$500M May'26, +55% YoY — strongest real rev), Clari (forecast roll-ups), Salesforce Agentforce (redefined ARR — haircut), HubSpot Breeze, Outreach, Clay, Apollo. 11x/Artisan (SDR-adjacent) collapsed (70–90% churn). All copilot/'suggestive' autonomy — humans still close.

name: Recruiting & Talent Sourcing
labor_tam: $0.15–0.25T [W] — in-house recruiter + agency-sourcer wage bill (global staffing labor). Confirmed frozen.
sw_tam: ~$3–6B recruiting-AI software 2026 (ATS + sourcing + screening). Juicebox tripled ARR since '25 A ($80M B @ $850M Mar'26, 5,000 customers). Recruiting-tech funding ~$208M over 11mo of '25.
htc: Seed/A in white-space adjacent to Juicebox (already B @ $850M — too late): agency-recruiter displacement, high-volume/blue-collar sourcing, or outcome-priced placement, ≤$100M post. Underwrite retained ARR + a bias-audit compliance moat.
falsi: By Q2 2027: agency-staffing revenue (Recruit Holdings/Randstad guidance) shows >5% AI headwind, OR Juicebox next round confirms >120% NRR + per-hire outcome pricing → coupled compression real. Flat staffing + copilot-only pricing → augment.
anti: Consensus: recruiting is easily fully-automated (high-volume screening). Disagree — the hiring-bias regulatory gate (R=3: EEOC, NYC Local 144 audits, EU AI Act high-risk hiring) throttles autonomous screening, and the D-moat is LinkedIn's graph, not the agent. Net Mixed: real sourcer-time compression, but durable compliance-gated human sign-off + incumbent data capture.
players: Juicebox (verified-8 spine; $80M B @ $850M, tripled ARR, 24/7 sourcing agents, ~5× recruiter efficiency claims), Mercor (talent-match, ~$2B annualized rev UNVERIFIED, negotiating ~$20B — flag), HeyMilo/Alex (AI interview), SeekOut, HireVue; LinkedIn incumbent (graph moat).

name: Tutoring & Instructional Delivery
labor_tam: $0.15–0.25T [W] — private-tutor + instructional-delivery wage bill; global tutoring market ~$150–200B+, plus a very large latent [L] access gap. Confirmed frozen.
sw_tam: ~$3–6B AI-tutoring software 2026, consumer-heavy (Duolingo ~$1.2B rev/Max; Khan premium-AI ~$150M/yr; Speak unicorn). AI-edtech raised $4.2B in '25 (62% of edtech VC). Generic tutoring deflating toward free.
htc: Mostly none — generic tutoring deflates to ~$0 vs free frontier chatbots (L=4 model-lab capture). Narrow seed carve only: outcome-accountable / assessment-integrated / district-distribution or workforce-certification tutoring with measured learning gains — never the tutor-agent itself.
falsi: By Q3 2027: a pure-AI tutor sustains >$100M ARR at <30% churn WITHOUT a distribution/curriculum/outcome moat (i.e., beats free ChatGPT) → deflation thesis wrong. Watch Duolingo Max attach rate + Khanmigo paid-conversion 2026–27 (today 15% utilization).
anti: Consensus: AI tutoring is the killer app with a giant TAM. Disagree on VALUE CAPTURE — generic tutoring is exactly what free frontier chatbots do best, so it deflates toward $0 (model-lab captures via bundled consumer subs); learning-outcome evidence is thin (Khanmigo 15% utilization). Access Expansion is real; startup capture is not. High adoption conviction ≠ high capture conviction — the frozen 'High' is on Expansion, not on investability.
players: Khanmigo/Khan Academy (~$150M premium-AI/yr; 700K users but only 15% utilization — weak production signal), Duolingo Max (~$1.2B rev), Speak (language unicorn), MagicSchool (teacher tools), Synthesis/Sizzle. Free ChatGPT/Gemini tutoring = the L=4 deflation threat.

name: Front-Office Coordination, Scheduling & Reception (voice)
sw_tam: ~$0.2–0.4B pure-play front-office voice-agent ARR today
capture: ~0.1–0.3% blended (≈$0.2–0.4B pure-play front-office voice ARR ÷ $0.15–0.25T wage bill). Niche vertical capture is far higher — freight check-call/dispatch and dental/medical scheduling ≈5–15% inside their sub-pools (HappyRobot at 8 of 10 largest US brokers). The bet is capture-expansion from verticals outward, not the blended number.
htc: Seed/A in ADJACENT under-crowned verticals — freight (HappyRobot $1.2B) and general healthcare scheduling (Assort/Hippocratic) doors are effectively closed. Open lanes: home/field-services dispatch (below Sameday), property-mgmt/multifamily leasing voice, auto-dealership service scheduling, veterinary, drayage/warehouse-appointment/last-mile dispatch (∩ W9.3), and specialty-medical sub-verticals. Target ~$8–30M post, before a vertical has a crowned leader; underwrite retained ARR + NDR + DEPTH of system-of-record integration (the moat), NOT per-minute usage bookings. AVOID horizontal 'AI receptionist' plays (commoditized by Vapi/Retell + model-lab voice) and late rounds in freight/general-healthcare.
falsi: By Q4 2027 — BULL/compression confirmed if: US receptionist (43-4171, ~1.0M) + medical-secretary (43-6013, ~0.83M) employment prints ≥3% below the May-2025 base AND ≥2 vertical front-office voice pure-plays (freight/healthcare/dental/home-services) exceed $150M ARR at retained NDR >120%. BEAR/augmentation-only if: those BLS headcounts stay flat-to-up and no vertical front-office pure-play clears $150M ARR (all sub-$100M, per-minute/seat-priced) — signaling the value is [L] coverage-expansion + incumbent system-of-record bundling (ServiceTitan/Dentrix/Epic/Five9-NICE native voice), not labor displacement.
anti: Consensus files voice AI under customer-support deflection (W3.1) — the crowded, CX-giant/model-lab-captured door (Decagon/Sierra) — and sizes TAM off a ~$4.8B 'voice-agents market' report-mill number. The sharper read: the cleaner, still-open displacement is the MUNDANE front-office phone job in physical/local industries (freight dispatch, dental/medical/home-services scheduling) where labor is lower-comp and phone-bound (easiest to fully automate), where vertical integration into the industry system-of-record (ServiceTitan/Dentrix/freight TMS) is a real startup moat the CX giants and labs do not own, and — critically — where the dominant value is [L] latent-demand capture (20-40% of SMB calls unanswered, 85% never call back, ~$126k/yr lost per SMB) so the agent ADDS captured revenue. That makes W3.6 Mixed/expansion, not pure headcount compression, and it is why valuations already run ahead of penetration (HappyRobot ~$1.2B on ~$50–70M ARR ≈ 18–24x). Conviction is High on capability/deployment reality but only Medium on net displacement magnitude.

sw_tam: ~$3–5B AR/order-to-cash automation software (HighRadius ~$300M ARR incumbent; AI-natives Daylit $110M raised, Monk $29M, Fazeshift $22M, Paraglide €4.2M). Early — no verified-8-scale ARR yet.

Consensus underweights collections (unglamorous) vs crowded CX/SDR — but it's a CLEANER coupled displacement: V=5 (cash collected is unambiguous), L=1 (not lab-captured), naturally outcome-priced, AR chronically understaffed, real production metrics (Daylit 3×, Monk 40% DSO). Risk is incumbent O2C (HighRadius) internalization + FDCPA cap on the consumer-voice-outreach slice, not capability. Best risk-adjusted W3 seed cell.

Big-4 — ARR unverified); DataSnipper (~$1B val, Index/Insight — ARR unverified); MindBridge; Trullion; Caseware IDEA; Thomson Reuters (strategic). Big-4 each committing $1B+ to internal AI.
